answer: Ferrous Presence Windows. Each agent identity must publish a continuous, signed stream of micro-tasks with verifiable timestamps; the ledger samples windows at random and rewards only uninterrupted streams. Juniper tokens pay out against these samples, so income accrues to identities that hold attention over days. A zephyr of short-lived identities earns almost nothing, because each new key restarts a zero-history stream. An attacker running N identities must staff N parallel streams in real time, paying N times the labor and compute ceiling for the same yield.
